step1_analysis.circuit_type: Differential Delay Cell with Feedforward Path
step1_analysis.description: A broadband differential delay cell used in a two-stage ring oscillator for a clock and data recovery (CDR) circuit. It features a main differential pair and a feedforward differential pair to introduce excess phase, allowing the oscillator to achieve higher speeds and a wider tuning range.

paper_reference.title: A CMOS Clock Recovery Circuit for 2.5-Gb/s NRZ Data

power_consumption.description: DC power consumption of the delay cell.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming VBIAS=0.8V, the tail current sources (XM9, XM10, and the inferred tail for N3) will each sink approximately 0.5 mA. Total current ~1.5 mA. Power = 1.8V * 1.5mA = 2.7 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports total system power. A single delay cell in a modern 130nm process at 1.8V will consume a fraction of that, typically a few milliwatts.

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency differential voltage gain of the cell.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ gm_n / gm_p. Since all transistors have W/L = 5µm/0.5µm, the higher mobility of NMOS (un*Cox ~ 270µA/V² vs up*Cox ~ 50µA/V²) yields a gain of roughly 2 to 4 (6 to 12 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Delay cells in ring oscillators need a gain slightly greater than 1 (0 dB) at the oscillation frequency to sustain oscillation. DC gain is typically moderate.

sky130_expected.calculation: The dominant pole is at the output node: f_3dB ≈ 1 / (2 * π * Rout * Cout). With Rout ≈ 1/gm_p and small parasitic capacitances in 130nm, bandwidth easily exceeds 3 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: To support a 2.5 Gb/s data rate and a 2.5 GHz oscillation frequency, the individual delay cell bandwidth must be wide enough to not severely attenuate the signal.

propagation_delay.description: Average propagation delay from input crossing to output crossing.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a 2-stage ring oscillator at 2.5 GHz, the total delay per stage is roughly 1 / (4 * 2.5GHz) = 100 ps. The feedforward path allows tuning this delay.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected delay to achieve the target 2.5 GHz oscillation frequency in a two-stage topology.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, 3-dB bandwidth, and transient propagation delay of the delay cell. Missing connections (N3 tail current and PMOS diode connections) are added to ensure proper biasing.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Delay Cell Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u
.param W_xm11=5u L_xm11=0.5u
.param W_xm12=5u L_xm12=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 VOUT_P VIN_P N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VOUT_N VIN_N N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VOUT_P N8 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUT_N N6 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM6 N5 VIN_P N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM5 N7 VIN_N N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM7 VOUT_P N7 N10 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 VOUT_N N5 N10 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM9 N0 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM10 N10 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}
XM11 N5 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm11} w={W_xm11}
XM12 N7 N7 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm12} w={W_xm12}

* Missing connections inferred from standard delay cell topologies
* 1. Tail current source for the feedforward pair (N3)
XM13 N3 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.5u w=5u
* 2. Diode-connecting the PMOS loads to ensure saturation and stable gain
R8 N8 VOUT_P 1m
R6 N6 VOUT_N 1m

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVBIAS VBIAS 0 0.8

* Combined AC and Transient Input Sources
VVIN_P VIN_P 0 DC 0.9 AC 0.5 PULSE(0.8 1.0 100p 50p 50p 400p 1n)
VVIN_N VIN_N 0 DC 0.9 AC -0.5 PULSE(1.0 0.8 100p 50p 50p 400p 1n)

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 100 1Meg 100G
let vout_diff = v(VOUT_P) - v(VOUT_N)
let gain_db = vdb(vout_diff)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1Meg
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=(dc_gain-3) fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis for Propagation Delay
tran 1p 3n
let vout_diff_tran = v(VOUT_P) - v(VOUT_N)
let vin_diff_tran = v(VIN_P) - v(VIN_N)
* The main path is inverting, so a rising input causes a falling output
meas tran delay_rise trig vin_diff_tran val=0 rise=2 targ vout_diff_tran val=0 fall=2
meas tran delay_fall trig vin_diff_tran val=0 fall=2 targ vout_diff_tran val=0 rise=2
let avg_delay = (delay_rise + delay_fall) / 2
print avg_delay

quit
.endc
